questions.q: SELECT Id, Name, Account.Industry FROM Contact returns what shape of result?
options: One row per Account, with a nested list of Contacts
One row per Contact, with the related Account's Industry flattened onto that same row
A separate result set for Contacts and a separate result set for Accounts
A runtime error, since relationship fields cannot appear in SELECT
questions.explain: Child-to-parent dot notation flattens the parent's field onto the same row as the child — one row per child record, not a nested structure.

questions.q: For a custom lookup field with API name Project__c, how do you traverse it as a relationship in SOQL?
options: Project.Lookup
Project__c
Project__Rel
Project__r
questions.explain: Custom relationship traversal replaces the __c suffix with __r — Project__c becomes Project__r when used as a relationship path in SOQL.

questions.q: If a query using a custom relationship name throws an 'invalid relationship' error, where should you check first?
options: The field's definition in Setup, to confirm its actual relationship name
The org's API version settings
The user's profile permissions
The Query Plan tool's cardinality output
questions.explain: A custom field's relationship name is configurable when the field is created and doesn't always match what you'd guess — Setup is where to confirm the actual name.

questions.q: SELECT Account.Owner.Name FROM Contact demonstrates what?
options: A semi-join
A parent-to-child subquery
Chaining dot notation across two relationship hops in a single query
An aggregate function applied to a relationship field
questions.explain: This traverses from Contact up to Account, then up again to that Account's Owner — two chained relationship hops in one dot-notation path.

questions.q: Why is needing to traverse three or more relationship levels deep in a single query worth pausing on?
options: SOQL enforces a hard limit of exactly one relationship level, making three levels impossible
It can signal the data model has unnecessary indirection, or that splitting into two queries joined in Apex would be clearer
It always triggers a governor limit violation regardless of how many records are returned
It automatically converts the query into a SOSL search
questions.explain: Very deep relationship chains are a maintainability smell even when technically within documented limits — not necessarily an error, but worth questioning.
